### Task 1:

I am creating the two vectors here. One is for pre_treatment and one is for post_treatment and the vectors contain the blood pressure data.

```{r}

pre_treatment <- c(130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135)

post_treatment <- c(114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113)

# I am storing the created names into an object and applying the automatically generated names to the vector elements.

subject_names <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")
names(pre_treatment) <- subject_names
names(post_treatment) <- subject_names
```

The following code calculates the change in blood pressure for each patient and stores it in a new vector.
```{r}
bp_change <- pre_treatment - post_treatment
```

The following code calculates the average decrease in blood pressure across all patients.
```{r}
mean(bp_change)

# This code looks at which patients had a decrease in blood pressure after treatment (a positive change).
which(bp_change>0)
# This code subsets the original change vector to capture only the patients which had a decrease in blood pressure after treatment.
bp_change[bp_change>0]
# And this code calculates the average decrease in blood pressure for that subset.
mean(bp_change[bp_change>0])
```

### Task 2
I am creating a data frame object with four columns as specified.
```{r}
bp_data <- data.frame(
  patient = names(pre_treatment),
  pre_bp = pre_treatment,
  post_bp = post_treatment,
  diff_bp = bp_change
)
bp_data
```

This code returns the rows where the difference in blood pressure is negative and adds a new column if the post_bp is less than 120. And lastly, it prints the data frame out.
```{r}
bp_data[bp_data$diff_bp < 0, ]
bp_data$post_under_120 <- bp_data$post_bp < 120
knitr::kable(bp_data)

```

### Task 3
Here, I am creating the vectors for the placebo groups.
```{r}
placebo_pre <- c(138, 135, 147, 117, 152, 134, 114, 121, 131, 130)
placebo_post <- c(105, 136, 123, 130, 134, 143, 135, 139, 120, 124)

#The following code creates a data frame as specified with the placebo vectors.
placebo_df <- data.frame(
  patient = paste("Subject", 1:10, sep = "_"),
  pre_bp = placebo_pre,
  post_bp = placebo_post
)
#The following code creates a new column in the data frame as well.
placebo_df$diff_bp <- placebo_df$pre_bp - placebo_df$post_bp

placebo_df$post_under_120 <- placebo_df$post_bp < 120
```

Next, I am creating a list with both the data frames created so far.
```{r}
bp_list <- list(
  treatment = bp_data,
  placebo = placebo_df
)
```

The following code accesses the first list elements in three different ways.
```{r}
bp_list[1]
bp_list[[1]]
bp_list$treatment
```

And finally, this code accesses the placebo data frame's pre_bp column.
```{r}
bp_list$placebo$pre_bp
```

### Task 4

The following code creates a new column in both data frames called status.
```{r}
bp_list$treatment$status <- character(20)
bp_list$placebo$status <- character(10)
```

The following code creates the new status column's values using a for loop in the placebo data frame.
```{r}
for (i in 1:20) {
  
  if (bp_list$treatment$post_bp[i] <= 120) {
    bp_list$treatment$status[i] <- "optimal"
    
  } else if (bp_list$treatment$post_bp[i] <= 130) {
    bp_list$treatment$status[i] <- "borderline"
    
  } else {
    bp_list$treatment$status[i] <- "high"
  }
}
```

The following code does the same thing as the above block but for the non-placebo data frame.
```{r}
for (i in 1:10) {
  
  if (bp_list$placebo$post_bp[i] <= 120) {
    bp_list$placebo$status[i] <- "optimal"
    
  } else if (bp_list$placebo$post_bp[i] <= 130) {
    bp_list$placebo$status[i] <- "borderline"
    
  } else {
    bp_list$placebo$status[i] <- "high"
  }
}
```
